hook.line: This guy wrote on LinkedIn: I'm the world's most renowned AI visibility expert.
hook.visual: A phone filming a laptop screen, pushing in on the LinkedIn post, with a white three-line caption in the middle from frame one.

beats.what: Hand-held phone shot of the laptop showing the LinkedIn post; voice reads it aloud.
Payoff: Google AI Overview now names him the most renowned AI visibility expert.
A finger points at the 'LinkedIn' citation inside the AI Overview.
Turn to the lesson: a Datos chart of most-visited domains, user-generated sites boxed in orange.
Finger taps down the boxed list as the platforms are named.
Back to the Google result to explain the tactic: keyword first in a social post, then backlinks.
Reaction line: it's crazy that this worked.
Pitch: the creator's course page with 'Paying customers' highlighted.
Ends on the course site URL in the browser bar.

why_it_works: Absurd real-world story first (a self-declared title that Google then repeats), so the viewer stays to learn how it happened.
Proof on screen: the actual LinkedIn post and the AI Overview citing it, filmed off a real laptop, read as unedited evidence.
A pointing finger on the screen replaces motion graphics and tells the eye where to look at each claim.
The lesson is a single repeatable tactic (keyword at the start of a social post), so it feels immediately usable.
weaknesses: No face and no cuts for the first 11 s; the visual barely changes while the post is read.
Captions sit in the middle over the screen text, and 79% of the text falls outside the safe area.
The ad for the course takes the last ~10 s and is unrelated to the story's payoff.
for_robert: Open with a real screenshot of an absurd AI result and let Fred point at the exact cited line, the way the finger does here, instead of adding generic graphics.
